reviews.text: 数值堆叠严重... 乐趣在demo大概半小时到这1.1小时之间消耗殆尽. 中期开始完全就是在拼双方数值... 如果不是拼数值那就产生了另一个尖锐的问题：猎场到底能不能挂机 如果能, 那么最终无非是敌人能不能一击必杀玩家的拼一击线, 回到上面数值堆叠的问题 如果不能, 那么猎场的杂兵和boss之间的巨大差距形成了一个玩家必须盯着镜头并随时准备与BOSS纠缠的状态, 既不是挂机也不是高压战斗, 卡在了一个不上不下的心流. 符合价格, 可堪一玩, 极小歼灭圈like的作品 在一些设计上有可圈可点之处, 但是远不及我demo里对作品的总体预期.

玩这个游戏就是为看看我适不适合poe like游戏，结论是不适合。放弃poe2 。 这个游戏前中期升级的体验其实还可以，但是到底了后期体验直线下降。 后期的玩法就是研究组各种bd打高难度，但是各种数据统计缺失，各种词缀算法不明确，词缀之间影响不明确，有些板子圣物效果不明确，导致我很难组好一个强力bd。 以我的例子，我50层狂怒，消耗狂怒每层总增2.7%的板子每一个 可以总增135%，看起来很高是把，但是使用多个此板子伤害并没有显著提高，难道同板子之间是加法？但是我换了一个纯粹板子，伤害显著提升，而且多个纯粹板子之间确实是乘算的。 总之类似的和其他情况的问题有很多。后期玩法很糟糕，自己研究尝试了多种bd最终伤害和生存都差不多。 后来我从网上搜了搜，发现高手的主要2种bd类型，一种是把3个技能的伤害几乎完美的乘起来，达到一个伤害很高的情况；另一种就是发现一个收益非常可观的伤害来源，狂堆加成，技能之间的伤害加成反而不高。但是作为一个单机游戏，我并不想抄bd，单机游戏还抄别人bd和云玩家也没区别，没有乐趣，可问题就是我并不能排除掉高手bd的情况下，靠自己组一个强度非常高的bd，这非常让人沮丧。 反思良久，以我暗黑系列游戏的体验和火炬之光，魔法工艺，失落城堡2，原点计划等游戏的对比，我发现装备制作系统的设计就是一条引导游戏走向死亡的不归路，是注定玩家群体小众的根本原因，是游戏销量杀手。而原因也很简单，装备制作没有乐趣，只有恶心。所以暗黑类游戏注定玩家多，而poe类游戏注定玩家少。当然这是对于广大普通玩家而言，至于那一小撮高手玩家与我何干？ 不得不提暗黑4的回火系统和洗词缀系统对于玩家而言也是非常糟糕的设计，毫无乐趣，只有恶心。学什么不好一定要学缺点（虽然可能对于日活时长等数据有利，但那是对开发公司而言）。 玩这个游戏就是因为poe2要来了，想先测试下自己能不能玩poe类游戏。非常遗憾，poe不适合我，普通玩家还是去玩暗黑类游戏吧。

装备机制有点恶心到我了 购买装备刷新机制要打三把，但你这三把很麻烦，要很久，地图也要买，还是刷新出来的？认真的？ 洗装备很麻烦，第一次见这么麻烦的 混沌装备升级合理么？升到混沌装备不能再洗属性？但你知道做好一个极品胚子需要多久？？？升胚子如果洗到不能再洗，这不崩溃？？？ 然后就是点开面板的时候敌人可以攻击，我攻击停止？？？认真的？一开界面就要心惊胆战的，怕突然暴毙！ 还有是不是应该做个统计面板了，很多伤害不明确。

So I was lured in by the free demo. Simple game play, surprisingly intricate interaction with skills. This was great. Bought the game for $10 (gamble based on graphics alone). And after 4 hours? In the current iteration I'm supremely disappointed. Max level is 50. Like they are doing a Borderlands thing where you only have X skill points to distribute across several different disciplines. But there aren't defined classes, so you effectively have to pick 1 of the 5 given to you, in order to be effective at anything. It offers a lot of skill customization, though most of the items you pick up WILL be garbage. As a ranger, I literally plopped myself in a corner and held down attack. My potion was always active. And killed everything. It's boring. I'd love to see a harder progression. Let us amass more skill points. Let us get higher levels. At $10... This is not worth the price point. I'd recommend this one sale only and after some refinement.

Dark Hunting Ground, developed by BingX and published by The Bueno Interactive, presents a compelling and streamlined take on the action RPG genre that emphasizes fast-paced combat, deep customization, and a rewarding loot-driven progression system. From the moment you step into its pixel-art world, the game immediately draws you into the role of a Hunter, a warrior tasked with battling the creeping Void and protecting your realm from its sinister influence. The game’s focus on accessible yet strategic gameplay makes it approachable for newcomers while still offering layers of complexity that will satisfy more experienced players. At its core, the gameplay loop in Dark Hunting Ground is straightforward but richly layered. You venture into procedurally generated hunting grounds where enemies become progressively tougher, and challenges escalate in intensity. Combat is fluid and responsive, relying heavily on the effective use of your chosen skills and weapons rather than just button mashing. What makes the experience stand out is how each build can be meticulously crafted through a wide variety of options. With six archetypes to choose from—Warrior, Assassin, Scholar, Ranger, Summoner, and Guardian—each character class brings unique playstyles and tactical possibilities. The ability to customize these builds with 18 core skills and 7 different Slates that alter abilities encourages experimentation and strategic thinking. One of the most satisfying aspects of Dark Hunting Ground is its loot and crafting systems. The game offers an extensive collection of over 80 relics, 60 Slates, and 35 Abyssal Eyes, each adding meaningful choices and powerful enhancements. This wealth of equipment allows you to tailor your character’s strengths, combining items to create devastating synergies or defensive bulwarks depending on your preferred playstyle. The crafting system’s deterministic nature means that you can refine your gear piece by piece, allowing for precise optimization without feeling locked into randomness. The automated looting options further streamline the gameplay, keeping the pace brisk and focused on combat rather than inventory micromanagement. As you progress, the game continually pushes you to adapt and refine your strategies. Boss encounters, which are challenging and often require a deep understanding of your build’s strengths and weaknesses, serve as milestones that test your mastery. Beyond the main hunting grounds, the Abyss mode introduces an endless survival challenge where waves of enemies test how long your build can endure under increasing pressure. This mode not only adds replayability but also provides valuable rewards, motivating players to push their limits and experiment with different builds. In addition to its core gameplay, Dark Hunting Ground offers a suite of quality-of-life features designed to enhance the player experience. Build presets allow quick swapping between different character setups, ideal for those who like to test various strategies. The training dummy feature is a thoughtful inclusion for players who want to measure their damage output and survivability, encouraging a more analytical approach to build refinement. The game also supports customizable keybinds, adjustable skill effect transparency, and options to skip repetitive reward screens, all contributing to a more polished and user-friendly experience. Visually, the game employs a minimalist pixel-art style that is both nostalgic and functional. The clear, crisp animations make combat easy to follow, even during hectic moments, and the varied enemy designs keep encounters visually interesting. While the graphics may not be groundbreaking, they perfectly complement the game’s emphasis on gameplay mechanics and strategic depth. The atmospheric soundtrack and sound effects further immerse players in the dark and foreboding world of the Void, adding emotional weight to the relentless hunting experience. Overall, Dark Hunting Ground excels at delivering a balanced mix of accessible action and deep customization. It doesn’t overwhelm players with complex lore or sprawling open worlds but instead hones in on the satisfying core of combat, build crafting, and progressive challenge. Whether you enjoy experimenting with different archetypes, optimizing your gear, or facing off against relentless foes, the game offers ample content and variety to keep you engaged. It stands as a solid entry in the indie action RPG space, promising long-term enjoyment through its continuous updates and evolving gameplay systems. For players looking for a focused, strategic, and rewarding hunting adventure, Dark Hunting Ground is a title worth diving into. Rating: 9/10

一款挂机类型的刷子游戏，27小时白金，19小时时剩下最后一个刷级成就，剩下8个小时就是挂机刷材料，刷的差不多了，打个20到30分钟靠多倍boss升下级。 以现在的情况来说，似乎是已经完成了除创意工坊外的所有更新。仔细的算了下，实际在操作的游玩时间应该是12小时左右，包括前期升阶，后期挂机后做装备。做装备简单，但需要挂机刷装备，一个是靠商店里刷新，这里不会出掉落限定词条，一个就是挂机掉落，掉落率低到发指，但以我的构筑来说，对掉落词条需求不高，且做装做一半已经可以挂机不死了，中期有次放着挂机去睡觉了，醒了看到活了接近5个小时，和一地装备，感觉应该是包满了，数量溢出卡我召唤物了，游戏难度并不算高。且终局基本没有内容，做装做好了除了成就就没有目标了。且作为终局内容，普通深渊成型很快，大概半小时到一小时就毕业了，无尽深渊没经验没掉落，只有一个分数奖励，摸完就不开了。 bd深度较浅，技能太少了。 吐槽一个意义不明的系统，装备制作，先不说随机词条，前期，需要掉落过才能制作，后期还需要局外点开制作橙装，并且制作需要20橙方块，同价位在商人那里可以买个红的，并且商人那里还能处理垃圾橙红，比分解收益高。升满500级都还剩一堆橙图纸点不满，不知道开着是做啥用的。 闲着没事的时候喜欢研究bd以及做装备刷装备可以买来玩玩，至少前中期乐趣不错。

To keep it as short as possible: 1- Gameplay loops till the end game, the first "main boss" you kill will be the same final boss you kill to complete the game 2- item crafting and stat rerolling in general are extremely tedious and were designed that way(no pity system builtin similar to a game like slormancer) 3- So many bugs and errors etc. (cant have a single session without atleast 1 blue screen crash, and ui or equipment features bugout when you reload back to your save so equipping/removing items bugout until it randomly fixes itself after playing for 5-10 more minutes) The gameplay formula is actually pretty fun, and it has alot of elements from other successful games of similar genres like path of exile for example, it just fails to deliver on QoL and a bug free gameplay experience. For it to be a great game it just needs the bugs/crashes fixed and a pity system put in to the crafting/rolling items systems and a slight numerical buffs to a few things to make some build archetypes that feel underwhelming in damage and scalability pop of a little bit more.

Surprisingly good, great to stall with in between different arpgs. You got 4 days to kill before a league launch? Boot it up. When it comes to the core talents, or in other words ascendancies/big class defining points, some feel massively stronger than others. For example, warrior has one that gives flat physical damage to melee skills equal to 25% of maximum life, that thing scales infinitely. Then we have let's say archer were all 3 picks for first core talent can basically be crafted on an item in the late endgame, nowhere close to the infinite warrior core talent. I'd say the two clearly strongest core talents by a mile is warriors life stuff, and assassins poison talents, maybe mages double mana cost for nova but yeah, many of the picks are really lacking since they are not unique, you can get 80% of the value from them as mods on engame items. You can get some cool items with drop only modifiers, so you have something to grind for, basically more multiplier mods instead of the usual %increase. It feels like it falls a tiny bit short, maybe 1 more step of progression would make it really satisfying, or 2 steps, and it would be great, but you sort of just win really really hard quite fast and then just grind for the love of the game. There is an infinite abyss where you go for highscores, and you get a skin after 10 000 000 score so I guess that is the "goal". There is a hard mode as well, so I guess you can play that for more challenge. There are a couple of different builds that got me itching to try them, knocked out life stacking on the first playthrough and now I'm going for some mana stacking. I'll be giving the poison stuff a spin as well later, if it works like I think it does then it might be bonkers.

For $6.50 it's fine, but the game hits a major bottleneck of boring grind once you get to Abyss Stars. I really enjoyed the theorycrafting in the first 50 levels of advancement. New relics and slates created new opportunities to improve your build. Eventually that all comes crashing to a halt when you hit level 50. After, you start getting these skull points that you cannot reallocate, so if you're like me and assumed they made permanent changes to your class and not just unlocked new features you then have to spend other skill points on, you make considerable early game mistakes to point allocation. Most of the points put into these features feel pointless anyway. You go from really solid passive skill trees to these things that make your shops mildly better... Woo... The repetitious grind of mobs to bosses to the chaotic boss gets very repetitive after you stop unlocking useful relics and slates. Then you have to farm Abyss Stars, which are rare drops during mob farming. Apparently there's one more new farming system after this and I can only imagine how tedious that one is. I like the Abyss Star rooms, too. They are harder and the chests at the end feel much more rewarding than normal drops. But I get like 1 star every 5-10 waves and that's painfully slow when the game was already slowing down too much for my liking. I want to go and change my build to try another, but gosh the teardown and set up of that would require a massive undertaking of reattribution. If the farming process felt better, I would be far more inclined to invest that kind of time (I have over 500 hours in Diablo 4 and 150 in PoE 2, so I'm not stranger to build crafting), but it doesn't. It's boring and lifeless. Minor gripe, but many of the systems are not explained well either. Low life is how much life? An entire boss-level passive upgrade is designed around low life but I have no idea how little life triggers that. There are a lot of missing tooltips like that. There is absolutely a good system underneath everything here and I look forward to a sequel to this game to see how it improves. But I can't see myself putting in anymore hours. The slog has gotten way too sloggy.
